name: Self-Generated In-Context Examples / Traj-Bootstrap (Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks)
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (poster; accepted). Earlier presented at the ICML 2025 PUT (Programmatic representations for agent learning) Workshop poster. Preprint: arXiv:2505.00234 (v1 May 2025; v3 16 May 2025). NOTE: the task brief listed 'arXiv 2501.00750 (OpenReview 2025)', but arXiv:2501.00750 is a different, unrelated paper ('Beyond Text: ... No-Code Platform' by Cheonsu Jeong); the correct identifier for this work is arXiv:2505.00234, OpenReview id WdL3O58gde.
authors_affiliation: Vishnu Sarukkai, Zhiqiang Xie, Kayvon Fatahalian (all Stanford University). Project supported by Roblox and Meta; API credits from OpenAI and together.ai.
code_url: https://github.com/VSAnimator/llm_self_improvement (linked as [Code] on the author homepage). Project page/blog: https://vsanimator.github.io/self_improvement/
task_domain: LLM agents for multi-step sequential decision-making: embodied/text-game (ALFWorld), interactive code/SQL (InterCode-SQL), and compositional crafting (Wordcraft). Framed as agentic decision-making, not single-shot QA.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent ReAct-style decision-making in sparse-reward POMDPs (S,O,A,T,R,gamma) where reward is binary success only at episode end (R=1 success, R=0 otherwise). The agent autonomously bootstraps its own performance via in-context learning without human knowledge engineering (no custom prompts, no curated examples, no specialized observation/action spaces). Assumptions: (1) the trajectory database D is initialized with a small (possibly empty) set of human-provided exemplars, (2) a descriptor of the action space is given, (3) the agent has access to a set of training tasks it can attempt. Two-phase: a training/collection phase where the agent attempts training tasks and grows the database, then a frozen test-time phase. The +DB-Curation and +Exemplar-Curation variants run N=5 parallel database instances (each driven by a separate agent), but the deployed agent itself is single-agent (population-based training is a training-time mechanism, not a multi-agent deployment).
what_is_retrieved: trajectories / experiences: the agent's own past successful trajectories (and trajectory segments / state windows). Each trajectory tau = (goal g, plan p, sequence of (observation o_t, reasoning r_t, action a_t), success s). Retrieved as in-context examples (demonstrations) at plan and per-step decision points.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes: retrieval targets a self-built database of the agent's own successful trajectories that grows during the training/collection phase. It is seeded by a small human-provided set, so the construction is hybrid (offline seed + online/test-time-induced growth), but the dominant grounding is a growing experience store, not a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking at each decision point (k=6 examples retrieved by averaged cosine distance). However the work elevates a database-construction objective beyond per-item top-k: D* = argmax_D E_{g~T}[Success(Agent(g,D,E,T))], i.e. it optimizes the COLLECTION's emergent quality (coverage, diversity, complementarity) via population-based DB-curation and value-function-like exemplar selection, rather than just ranking individual items. Retrieval itself is still fixed-size top-k; the curation operates on which items populate the index.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve + partial Retain. Retrieve: dense top-k of past trajectories at each decision point. Reuse: trajectories used as verbatim ICL exemplars (no explicit case adaptation). Revise: not implemented (retrieved trajectories are not adapted/edited per case). Retain: yes - successful trajectories are stored, and exemplar-level curation selectively retains high-utility trajectories. So coverage is approximately [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes (verbatim), Revise: no, Retain: yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed via in-context learning, reward-weighted regression, population-based training (PBT), and value-function analogies from RL. It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain CBR mechanisms under another name.
retrieval_unit: Two-level: (1) full trajectory (problem-solution episode: goal, plan, and the (obs, reasoning, action) sequence) selected by trajectory-level keys; (2) sub-trajectory / state-window: within the top trajectories, a windowed slice of states (window of 5 steps around the most similar state) is selected for state-level retrieval. Thus the retrieved unit ranges from full trajectory (for plan-level retrieval) to a sub-trajectory/state-window segment (for per-step retrieval).
index_source: Growing, online/test-time-induced store seeded by a small offline human-provided exemplar set. The database D is built by the agent itself during the training/collection phase as it successfully completes tasks (online growth). Hybrid construction: human-seed (offline) + self-generated successful trajectories (online).
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over example embeddings, implemented with FAISS (exact nearest-neighbor search). Multi-key/context-keyed: separate keys per field (goal, plan, observation, reasoning) with hybrid search returning top-k by averaged cosine distance across keys, plus a sliding-window state-level index within trajectories. No graph or category hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense retriever using off-the-shelf sentence embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Sentence-BERT) with FAISS exact nearest-neighbor search and cosine similarity. Not learned/RL-trained; not BM25; not generative.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings; fixed cosine top-k). The LEARNING/selection signal is applied to the index contents, not the retriever: (a) +DB-Curation uses downstream-task effectiveness (recent training-task success rate) in a population-based-training loop to propagate good databases; (b) +Exemplar-Curation computes a retrieval-weighted quality metric Q(tau) (analogous to a value function) measuring each trajectory's empirical contribution to successful outcomes when retrieved, to keep high-utility exemplars. So the curation signal is downstream-task-effectiveness / value-based, but the embedding retriever has no learning signal.
query_construction: Raw, decision-point-conditioned keys. At plan time the key is the raw goal g. At step t, retrieval keys are [g, p, o_t] (goal, plan, current observation) for the pre-reasoning retrieval and [g, p, r_t] (goal, plan, current reasoning) for the pre-action retrieval, embedded directly with the same sentence encoder. Queries are the agent's own current context strings (no synthetic query generation, no decomposition).
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level (two-level retrieval): a task-level retrieval at plan time (key=goal), and fresh per-step retrievals at each decision point conditioned on current observation/reasoning, plus a within-trajectory state-level (windowed) retrieval. This dynamic per-decision retrieval is contrasted with using the same fixed examples throughout an episode.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step: retrieval is performed on a fixed schedule at every decision point of the ReAct loop (once for the plan, and at each timestep before reasoning and before action). It is not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router-gated.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the agent control loop: retrieve once at plan generation (key=goal), then at every timestep t retrieve before reasoning (keys=[g,p,o_t]) and before acting (keys=[g,p,r_t]). No confidence/attention/uncertainty/reflection-token trigger; retrieval frequency is determined by the agent's reason-act steps.
reranking: None - no separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder, no RRF). Candidates are scored by averaged cosine similarity across keys and the top-k are taken directly; for state-level retrieval a sliding window is added around the single most-similar state.
retrieved_context_refinement: Light structural refinement rather than content distillation: (1) multi-key averaged-similarity selection of trajectories; (2) a sliding-window extraction of a coherent +/-window-5 state segment around the most relevant state to provide coherent episode fragments. No decompose-recompose, distillation into rules, distractor filtering, or compression of the trajectory text itself.
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skill descriptions are indexed; the retrieved items are natural-language trajectory strings encoded with off-the-shelf embeddings (no docstring/synthetic-query/weighted-field engineering).
index_content_separation: N/A - no progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-heavy-content split; the embedded keys and the in-context example content are drawn from the same trajectory records. (A sliding window does limit how much of a trajectory's state content is injected.)
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - not a tool-retrieval system; no live tool index or RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling protocol. The store is an internally-managed FAISS index that grows as the agent solves tasks.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools retrieved).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved trajectories / state-window segments are inserted verbatim into the LLM prompts as in-context demonstrations at three call sites - LLM_plan(g, C_p), LLM_reason(tau, o_t, C_t), and LLM_act(tau, o_t, r_t, C_{t+1}) - formatted as goal->plan, goal,plan,observation,reasoning,action exemplars matching the requested output. The same self-collected data is also (in an appendix study) usable as fine-tuning data, but the core method is in-context (no weight updates at deployment).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-act, interleaved per decision point within a ReAct loop: a plan is first generated using goal-conditioned retrieved exemplars, then at each timestep the agent retrieves fresh examples before reasoning and before acting (Algorithm 1). No MCTS/tree search; the planning step is optional and omitted on short-horizon benchmarks (InterCode-SQL, Wordcraft) following RAP, and kept for long-horizon ALFWorld (~30 steps).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step / per-decision-point: retrieval is woven in at the plan step and at each reason and act step of the rollout (i.e., per reasoning step and per action within an episode), not merely once per final answer.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar - retrieved trajectories/segments are used as-is as demonstrations; there is no LLM-prompted case rewriting, execution-feedback revision, or critic-guided adaptation of the retrieved case. (Curation operates on which cases are stored/retained, not on adapting an individual retrieved case.)
retrieved_item_representation: Raw trajectory (and raw state-window segment) injected as natural-language goal/plan/(observation,reasoning,action) text. No distillation into strategies, rules, or guidelines; no executable program/skill abstraction; no latent/soft tokens. (This is explicitly contrasted with rule-distilling baselines like AutoGuide.)
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory / raw sub-trajectory (concrete past episode text), at the low (least-abstracted) end of the spectrum - deliberately NOT a distilled strategy/insight, state-aware rule, reusable workflow, or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Curation-based data quality control rather than retriever-side noise handling: (1) success-only filtering (only s=1 trajectories are stored, akin to reward-weighted regression); (2) +Exemplar-Curation drops trajectories whose retrieval-weighted utility Q(tau) is low (those that 'succeed in spite of bad decisions' that would be harmful to repeat), keeping only top-1 utility trajectory per task; (3) +DB-Curation removes underperforming whole databases. The retrieval step itself has no relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware training.
memory_type: Episodic experience memory (a database of self-generated successful trajectories). Stored as raw episodic trajectories, not a distilled skill-library/workflow/graph/latent memory.
write_back: True - successful trajectories generated by the agent are written into the database D and become retrievable in-context examples for future tasks, creating a positive feedback loop (successful examples help solve new tasks, generating more successful examples).
online_growth: True - the retrievable store grows during the training/collection phase as the agent attempts and solves training tasks (database scaling is a central studied axis; performance improves with more training tasks, with diminishing returns after ~25% of tasks). The database is then frozen for the reported test-time evaluation (test-time cost is identical across methods).
write_back_trigger: On-success only: a trajectory is written to the database iff the episode succeeds (s=1). Failed trajectories are NOT stored, due to the credit-attribution problem of identifying good vs bad sub-segments. For the curation variants, additional write-time selection occurs: +DB-Curation events fire at size thresholds (10, 20, 40, 80, ... doublings) replacing the bottom-20% database with copies of the top-20%; +Exemplar-Curation selects the top-1 utility trajectory per task into a composite database after training.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only. Failed trajectories are explicitly excluded from the database (paper notes failures are harder to operationalize due to credit attribution and leaves leveraging them for exploration to future work). Negative/contrastive failure storage is not used. Implicitly, exemplar-level curation down-weights/removes 'successful' trajectories that empirically lead to downstream failures (low Q), but it does not store failed trajectories as corrective cases.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only growth plus prune/replace curation. Base Traj-Bootstrap is append-only (successful trajectories accumulate). +DB-Curation does forget-and-propagate at the database level (replace worst databases with copies of best in a population-based-training loop). +Exemplar-Curation does forget-prune at the exemplar level (retain only top-1 utility trajectory per task into a composite DB). Individual stored trajectories are not mutated/rewritten in place (no delta-update or refine-overwrite of an entry's content).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No for the retrieval step itself (fixed off-the-shelf cosine top-k, not a learned/RL retrieval policy). However, index curation is cast in RL-analogy terms: +DB-Curation = population-based training (selection of database 'genomes' by recent success), +Exemplar-Curation = a value-function-like quality metric Q(tau) estimating each trajectory's contribution to success. These are selection heuristics inspired by RL, not a trained soft-Q/M-MDP retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Within a training run, N=5 parallel database instances (each with its own agent) share/propagate experience via population-based DB-curation (copying high-performing databases) and via exemplar-curation that pools trajectories across all N databases into a composite DB. This is collective memory across parallel agent instances of the SAME framework, not cross-heterogeneous-framework sharing. The method is also model-agnostic/portable (same database usable across LLMs; demonstrated improving even a fine-tuned agent in an appendix).
benchmarks: ALFWorld (text-based embodied navigation/object manipulation), InterCode-SQL (interactive SQL coding environment), and Wordcraft (Little-Alchemy-style compositional element-crafting). Comparison baselines drawn from ALFWorld evaluations of AutoGuide and AutoManual.
benchmark_family: Embodied (ALFWorld) + code/interactive-coding (InterCode-SQL) + compositional-reasoning game (Wordcraft). Spans the embodied and code families (with a game/decision benchmark), under sparse-reward sequential decision-making.
baselines: Fixed-DB (the same ReAct agent with a fixed human-provided initial example database and no growth) is the primary internal baseline. External/contextual comparisons on ALFWorld: AutoGuide (Fu et al. 2024, converts successful trajectories into explicit rules + retrieves rules, gpt-3.5-turbo+gpt-4-turbo) and AutoManual (Chen et al. 2024, hand-crafted task-specific observation/action spaces + manual generation, gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4-turbo+gpt-4o-mini). Also contextualized against test-time scaling (Fixed-DB pass@k, k=1..5) and against LLM upgrade (gpt-4o-mini -> gpt-4o). Conceptually positioned against ExpeL, RAP, TRAD.
key_metrics: Task success rate (binary, averaged over test tasks, mean +/- std over 5 trials) on all three benchmarks; pass@k of the Fixed-DB baseline for the test-time-scaling comparison; AUROC of a success-prediction classifier in the diagnostics analysis (0.77 InterCode-SQL, 0.71 Wordcraft).
headline_result: On ALFWorld, +DB+Exemplar-Curation reaches 93% success (0.93 +/- 0.03) with gpt-4o-mini, surpassing AutoManual (0.91, which uses gpt-4-turbo+gpt-4o-mini and hand-crafted observation/action spaces) and AutoGuide (0.79*). Even naive Traj-Bootstrap raises ALFWorld 73%->89%, Wordcraft 55%->64%, InterCode-SQL 75%->79%; the ALFWorld gain exceeds the boost from upgrading gpt-4o-mini->gpt-4o and matches Fixed-DB pass@3 (single attempt).
ablations: (1) Method decomposition (Table 1): Fixed-DB vs Traj-Bootstrap vs +DB-Curation vs +Exemplar-Curation vs +DB+Exemplar-Curation across all three benchmarks - shows naive accumulation gives the largest single jump, +Exemplar-Curation best on Wordcraft (0.72), +DB+Exemplar-Curation best on ALFWorld (0.93) and InterCode-SQL (0.82). (2) Database scaling (Fig.2): success rises with number of training tasks (100 -> 3500) with diminishing returns past ~25%, since each new example is retrieved less often as DB grows. (3) 'Best vs worst' exemplar selection (Fig.4): selecting top-1 vs bottom-1 trajectory by Q(tau) confirms the utility metric - 'best' (=+Exemplar-Curation) beats 'worst' on ALFWorld and Wordcraft. (4) Test-time-scaling comparison (Table 3): Traj-Bootstrap ~= Fixed-DB pass@2-3, +DB+Exemplar-Curation ~= pass@3-5. (5) LLM-upgrade comparison (Table 2). (6) Appendix: fine-tuning on self-collected data; success-prediction classifier (AUROC).
evaluation_decoupling: No - the paper reports end-to-end task success rate (and pass@k, AUROC for diagnostics), but does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) decoupled from task performance. The exemplar-utility metric Q(tau) is a curation signal, not a reported retrieval-quality benchmark.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-focused (final binary task success). Some process-adjacent analyses: training-task rolling success used for curation, the retrieval-weighted exemplar quality Q(tau), and the success-prediction classifier (AUROC) that probes whether outcomes are predictable from goal/observation embeddings. No step-wise retrieval-accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Train-time vs test-time tradeoff is explicit: +DB-Curation and +Exemplar-Curation require N=5x more LLM inference calls during TRAINING (5 parallel database instances) but use the SAME number of training tasks; at TEST time all three methods have identical computational cost (Algorithm 1 is just given a different database D), contrasting with per-task test-time sampling methods. Gains match Fixed-DB pass@2-5 without extra test-time attempts. No explicit wall-clock/latency/dollar figures reported beyond call-count scaling. [uncertain on exact API-cost/latency numbers]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: k=6 examples retrieved per decision point (stated as k=6). State-level retrieval uses a sliding window of 5 steps around the most-similar state to bound injected content. No explicit token-budget cap stated; selection is fixed-k top-k by averaged cosine distance (not adaptive/precision-driven, not reranked-then-truncated).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - uses existing benchmarks (ALFWorld, InterCode-SQL, Wordcraft); not a benchmark-construction paper. Database scaling experiments use up to 3500 training tasks on ALFWorld; results averaged over 5 trials. [uncertain on exact per-benchmark train/test split sizes]
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) as the base agent loop; retrieval-augmented agent example-selection from RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024) and TRAD (Zhou et al. 2024, step-wise thought retrieval); reward-weighted regression (Peters & Schaal) for success-only filtering; population-based training (Jaderberg et al. 2017) for DB-curation; value-function learning (RL) analogy for the exemplar quality metric; many-shot ICL scaling (Agarwal et al. 2024; Bertsch et al.); Sentence-BERT / all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Reimers & Gurevych) and FAISS (Douze et al.) for retrieval; DSPy (Khattab et al.) for automatic example curation context; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) as an experiential-learning predecessor.
contrasts_with: AutoManual (hand-crafted task-specific observation/action spaces + generated manuals) and AutoGuide (distills trajectories into explicit context-aware rules) - both use task-specific knowledge engineering and/or rule abstraction; this work instead retains RAW self-generated trajectories with no abstraction or task-specific engineering. Also contrasted with: test-time sampling / multiple-attempt (pass@k) methods (shifts compute to train-time instead), LLM upgrades, RL/fine-tuning-based self-improvement (DPO, RLHF, o1), and methods using fixed per-task examples throughout an episode (vs dynamic per-decision-point retrieval).
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval) intersecting experiential/episodic-memory agent self-improvement. Lineage: ReAct -> retrieval-augmented exemplar agents (RAP, TRAD) and experiential learners (ExpeL, AutoGuide, AutoManual) -> Traj-Bootstrap, which pushes toward fully self-generated, raw-trajectory in-context databases with population-level (PBT) and exemplar-level (value-function-style) utility curation, emphasizing data-centric scaling of test-time-collected experience over architectural or task-specific engineering.
